title: Lift regular closed-fibre kernel parameters preserving the base regular sequence
statement: Let R and S be regular local rings, E a regular local ring, u:R→S and v:S→E local ring maps, and v surjective. Suppose v annihilates m_R S, the images of some regular system of parameters of R extend to a regular system of parameters of S, and S/m_R S is regular local. Then there is a proper ideal J of S with ker(v)=J+m_R S and a regular system of parameters t of R whose images form a regular sequence on S/J. No completeness or formal smoothness is assumed or concluded.

source.place: Tag 07NR, proof, first two paragraphs; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NR

proof.text: Choose the parameter lists t,z from the hypothesis, put a=t.map(u) and I=m_R S=Ideal.ofList(a), and descend v to the surjection w:S/I→E. Its kernel quotient is ring-isomorphic to E, so it is regular local. Apply the initial-quotient assertion of the regular-sequence theorem to a++z: S/I has dimension length(z). Apply the regular-local quotient kernel parameter theorem to w to obtain a full parameter list bs of S/I and c with ker(w)=Ideal.ofList(bs.take(c)).

source.place: Tag 07NR, proof, first two paragraphs; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NR

proof.text: Lift the entire list bs to a list ys in S via surjectivity of the quotient map q. The ideal generated by a++ys contains I and maps to the maximal ideal of S/I. The maximal ideal of S also maps to that maximal ideal and contains I. Comapping both equalities proves that a++ys generates the maximal ideal of S. Its length equals length(a)+length(z), since the parameter list bs has length equal to dim(S/I). Thus a++ys is a regular system of parameters. This elementary ideal argument replaces the cotangent-basis extension and Nakayama steps. The Mathlib facts used are map_maximalIdeal_of_surjective, comap_map_mk, map_ofList and list_map.

source.place: Tag 07NR, proof, first two paragraphs; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NR

proof.text: Put x=ys.take(c), b=ys.drop(c), and J=Ideal.ofList(x). The image of J under q is ker(w). The kernel formula for a quotient lift and comap_map_quotientMk give ker(v)=J⊔I. Since x is drawn from the parameter list a++ys, J lies in the maximal ideal and is proper. Permute the regular parameter list into x++(a++b). The regular-sequence theorem makes this list regular and S/J regular local. Mathlib isWeaklyRegular_append_iff first gives weak regularity of a++b on S/J (transporting through Submodule.quotEquivOfEq and isWeaklyRegular_map_algebraMap_iff), then weak regularity of its initial sublist a. The images of a lie in the maximal ideal of S/J, so IsRegular.of_isWeaklyRegular_of_mem_maximalIdeal makes a regular there. List.map_map identifies this list with the images of t under the composite R→S→S/J. All operations apply to empty lists as well.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_regular_fiber_kernel_parameter_quotient
    (R S : Type u) (E : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing E]
    [IsRegularLocalRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing S] [IsRegularLocalRing E]
    (u : R →+* S) (v : S →+* E) [IsLocalHom u] [IsLocalHom v]
    (hv : Function.Surjective v)
    (hkill : (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map u ≤ RingHom.ker v)
    (hparams : ∃ (t : List R) (z : List S),
      IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters t ∧
      IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (t.map u ++ z))
    (hfiber : IsRegularLocalRing (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map u)) :
    ∃ J : Ideal S, J ≠ ⊤ ∧
      RingHom.ker v = J ⊔ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map u ∧
      ∃ t : List R, IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters t ∧
        RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (S ⧸ J)
          (t.map ((Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp u))
